bounded_slice.candidate: Context binding for the candidate-set completeness commitment under prefix-free canonical encoding.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Local deterministic symbolic replay only, extending p1-sa-597. The trusted commitment authenticates a canonical manifest of sorted candidate digests. Tested whether generation, predecessor_digest, protocol/hash/canonicalization identifiers and candidate_count are required to prevent context replay. No public-source fetch, actual hash/signature computation, hosted coordinator, protected/manual execution, secret persistence, scheduler mutation or second semantic leaf.

model.baseline: Cset = H(Context || EncodePF(sorted(candidate_digests))) where EncodePF is a uniquely decodable prefix-free canonical list encoding.
model.security_goal: A commitment valid for one fork decision context must not be reusable as proof of completeness for a distinct generation, predecessor or protocol/interpretation context; the encoded candidate sequence must have one parse.
model.minimum_context: Bind enough trusted context to uniquely identify the fork generation, parent/predecessor and verification/selection protocol suite. Separate algorithm/canonicalization fields are not intrinsically required if one domain/suite identifier already fixes them uniquely.

necessity_matrix.result: necessary in this symbolic model unless already cryptographically bound by every candidate and verified from revealed candidate content
necessity_matrix.counterexample: If generation is omitted, the same candidate-digest sequence and predecessor can reproduce the same Cset when replayed as another generation, so the commitment alone does not prove which generation's complete set was committed.

necessity_matrix.result: necessary in this symbolic model unless the candidate digest definition already binds and the verifier checks the common predecessor
necessity_matrix.counterexample: If predecessor is omitted, an identical presented candidate-digest set can be replayed as completeness evidence for a different parent. Binding predecessor makes cross-parent substitution change the committed context.

necessity_matrix.result: necessary unless the verifier's trusted domain already fixes fork-choice rule, digest algorithm and canonical parser uniquely
necessity_matrix.counterexample: Without protocol/domain binding, identical candidate bytes can be carried into a different protocol version or interpretation whose selection rule or digest/canonicalization semantics differ, while Cset still matches the raw sequence.

necessity_matrix.condition: Redundant when a single bound protocol/suite/domain identifier uniquely fixes the candidate-digest algorithm and digest length; otherwise bind it or equivalent suite metadata to prevent algorithm-substitution ambiguity.

necessity_matrix.result: conditionally redundant under the requested prefix-free canonical assumption
necessity_matrix.condition: Redundant when the bound protocol/suite identifier uniquely fixes EncodePF and the verifier rejects every noncanonical representation; otherwise an encoding/version identifier or equivalent domain separation is required.

necessity_matrix.result: logically redundant under uniquely decodable prefix-free canonical list encoding
necessity_matrix.reason: The verifier parses EncodePF into exactly one candidate sequence and derives its length. An explicit count adds a consistency check but no additional set identity. If retained, it must equal the parsed length or the package is rejected.

canonicalization_tests.reason: Commitment equality cannot distinguish generation context.
Commitment equality cannot distinguish parent context unless parent is guaranteed inside verified candidate commitments.
Raw candidate-sequence commitment does not authenticate the interpretation or fork-choice rule.
Unique parse recovers the exact candidate sequence and therefore its count; no second sequence with a different count shares the same canonical byte string.
The suite/domain identifier already supplies equivalent context; repeating deterministic parameters inside the manifest is redundant rather than security-essential.

result.observation: The completeness digest must authenticate context, not merely the candidate bytes. Generation and predecessor are independent replay dimensions unless those facts are already guaranteed by verified candidate commitments. Protocol interpretation must also be domain-bound, but multiple parameter IDs can collapse into one suite identifier.
result.inference: A minimal symbolic manifest is DomainSuite || generation || predecessor_digest || EncodePF(sorted(candidate_digests)), where DomainSuite uniquely fixes fork-choice rule, digest algorithm and canonical encoding. candidate_count is derivable and therefore not logically necessary under prefix-free canonical encoding; it may remain as a checked redundancy field.
result.package_completeness: pass for the exact symbolic context-binding property only when the verifier authenticates generation, predecessor and a protocol/suite domain plus the uniquely parsed complete candidate sequence.
result.replayability: cross-generation and cross-parent replay are blocked by explicit context binding; cross-protocol interpretation replay is blocked by the bound suite/domain. No claim is made about the trustworthiness of the external commitment source.
result.hidden_executor_absence: pass for this exact symbolic slice: local deterministic reasoning plus lightweight repository state/evidence transport only
result.quota_zero_assessment: The symbolic context-binding check needs no hosted runner, Codespaces, cloud compute/storage, paid API/model, artifact service or finite credit. Repository transport is state/evidence persistence only; rate-limit recovery remains cross-invocation.
result.conflict_check: CLEAN-safe: semantically consumed only frozen sanitized controls and own scientist_agents LATEST/p1-sa-597. No O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, protected-primary, manual-user or scheduler semantics were used.
